cards.title: Verify each store-setup step on the live storefront
cards.summary: Adding a verification step after every mechanical store configuration task so a click path that 'looked done' is proven to actually work.
cards.use_when: Any time you complete a store setup task — theme code, product, payment, shipping profile or tax — before moving to the next setup item.

cards.title: Inject custom Liquid sections into a Shopify theme
cards.summary: Mechanical click path for adding a custom Liquid section file to a Shopify theme so a bespoke product page can be built manually.
cards.use_when: You need to build a custom PDP section or page by hand in Shopify (no page builder), e.g. a branded product template for a new SKU.

cards.title: Assign a custom page template to a specific product
cards.summary: Click path for creating a product-specific template in the theme customizer and pointing one product at it so it renders a custom Liquid section.
cards.use_when: You want one hero/paid-traffic product to have a unique PDP layout while all other products keep the default template.

cards.title: Make a product actually buyable before launch
cards.summary: The minimum product-admin steps to stop a new product from showing sold out or unaddable-to-cart at launch.
cards.use_when: Immediately before driving paid traffic or launch content to a new product, to avoid wasting spend on an unbuyable PDP.

cards.title: Reverse-engineer a validated product via a challenger angle
cards.summary: Score a candidate product across demand, ad momentum, store-level and competition signals, then only pursue it with a differentiating brand/content angle rather than a clone.
cards.use_when: Product selection: deciding whether to base a new store on a proven seller you found in ad libraries.

cards.title: Capture competitor pages and ads as structured research inputs
cards.summary: Use screenshots of a proven competitor page as the seed input to product validation, branding, mockups and page-mirroring workflows.
cards.use_when: Starting any reverse-engineering workflow (validation, branding, product mockup, page clone) and needing a clean source image of the target brand page.

cards.title: Build the brand kit before the store: intake, positioning and naming
cards.summary: Sequence for generating a usable brand system (strategy, voice, palette, logo, name) from a modeled competitor using an AI branding workflow.
cards.use_when: Building a new store's brand from scratch when you already have a validated product and a competitor to model.

cards.title: Generate a brand board, then lock it for production consistency
cards.summary: Use a generative image tool to explore a brand board, then move it into a precise design tool to freeze logo and palette for suppliers and print.
cards.use_when: Preparing brand assets before sending a logo or packaging to a supplier or designer, or building landing-page visuals on-brand.

cards.title: Write a brand reference guide for every downstream asset creator
cards.summary: Produce a short written brand description so mockups, product photography prompts and any hired creator can stay on-brand.
cards.use_when: Briefing product mockup generation, a photographer/videographer, or a designer and needing one consistent description of what the brand stands for.

cards.title: Draft the product mockup before contacting any supplier
cards.summary: Sequence for producing approved bottle and packaging mockups plus a clean pack shot from a competitor photo, logo, brand board and brand guide.
cards.use_when: Product sourcing and packaging prep: you need a visual target to send a supplier and to populate PDP imagery.

cards.title: Create on-brand lifestyle imagery from competitor inspiration
cards.summary: Adapt competitor lifestyle shot compositions into your own branded images by pairing an inspiration image with your product reference and a written prompt.
cards.use_when: Building PDP, landing-page and ad creative imagery that looks on-brand without a photoshoot.

cards.title: Sequence sourcing modes: dropship, then faster fulfillment, then private label
cards.summary: A staged sourcing recommendation: start dropshipping to test demand, upgrade fulfillment for speed, then move to private-label inventory as volume proves out.
cards.use_when: Choosing fulfillment/sourcing model for a new store built around a validated product, especially when launch capital is limited.

cards.title: Mirror a proven competitor page into your brand as a starting structure
cards.summary: Use a page-mirroring tool to replicate a high-performing competitor page's section structure, then rebrand it to your palette and logo.
cards.use_when: Building a homepage, collection page or PDP for a new brand when you have a proven competitor page to model and no page-builder available.

cards.title: Score and upgrade a mirrored page section-by-section
cards.summary: Audit a page against a scoring model, then add the missing sections it recommends rather than shipping the mirrored structure unchanged.
cards.use_when: Pre-launch page review: improving a PDP or homepage before spending on acquisition.

cards.title: Score a Product Page Against a High-Converting Template and Fill the Gaps
cards.summary: Use an AI page scorer to grade a PDP out of 100, then auto-inject the missing sections a proven high-converting page would have.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing product page or deciding which sections a new PDP needs before launch.

cards.title: The Four Objection-Covering Sections Every PDP Should Consider
cards.summary: Guarantee, how-it-works, us-versus-them, and founder-credibility sections each answer a specific reason shoppers hesitate.
cards.use_when: Deciding what content blocks to add to a product page that feels thin or isn't converting.

cards.title: Feed the Copywriter Raw Product Data for Better PDP Copy
cards.summary: AI PDP copy quality scales with the amount and specificity of product input you paste in, not with prompt cleverness.
cards.use_when: Generating product descriptions, benefit copy, FAQ text, or section headings for a new or refreshed product page.

cards.title: Publish a Custom PDP into Shopify as a Reusable Section
cards.summary: Ship a designed product page into Shopify by pasting the generated code as a Liquid section file, then adding it to a product template.
cards.use_when: Moving a page built in an external page designer into a live Shopify store.

cards.title: Update a Live Shopify Section Without Rebuilding the Page
cards.summary: Re-publish just the changed section code and paste it back into the existing Liquid file to push edits live.
cards.use_when: Fixing or improving one block (e.g. a broken accordion) on an already-published PDP.

cards.title: Generate On-Brand Product and Lifestyle Images with AI Assistants
cards.summary: Use specialised AI image workflows — brand-styled mimicry, prompt generation, and customer-experience scenes — to build a full PDP asset set.
cards.use_when: Producing hero images, ingredient/lifestyle shots, and customer-use imagery for a product page or ad creative.

cards.title: Product Page Template Standardisation as an Output, Not the Goal
cards.summary: The section-based approach trades some design uniqueness for speed and repeatability across many products.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build each PDP from scratch or reuse a section library for a multi-SKU store or a white-label brand launch.

cards.title: Use a Competitor PDP as the Reference Target for a New Build
cards.summary: Anchor your page spec to the sections, flow and proof a proven competitor page already uses, then fill the gaps they miss.
cards.use_when: Planning a PDP for a new product where you lack your own conversion data.

cards.title: Configure Purchase Options and Inventory So the Page Can Actually Sell
cards.summary: Subscription, bundle and inventory settings on the product decide what the PDP offers and whether it renders as purchasable.
cards.use_when: Finalising a new product listing before launching traffic to the PDP.

cards.title: Inspect the Guest-View Page Before Launching Traffic
cards.summary: Load the finished PDP in an incognito window to see the unbranded, logged-out experience your visitors will get.
cards.use_when: Final QA pass on a PDP, landing page or store before running ads or sending traffic.

cards.title: Set Up a Local AI Coding Environment for Shopify Theme Edits
cards.summary: Prepare an AI coding workspace for Shopify theme work, checking current tool access and editing an unpublished theme copy.
cards.use_when: You want to make custom theme or product-page edits (new blocks, modified cart, custom templates) without hiring a developer or adding apps.

cards.title: Connect Shopify CLI and Authenticate Your Store
cards.summary: Have Claude install the Shopify CLI (NPM version) and authenticate your store so it can list and pull themes.
cards.use_when: Your local Claude/VS Code environment is set up but not yet connected to your Shopify store, so you need it to see and pull themes.

cards.title: Duplicate the Live Theme Before Any AI Editing
cards.summary: Create a copy of the live theme and confine all edits to that copy to avoid breaking the storefront.
cards.use_when: You are about to make any AI-driven theme change and need a safe staging environment.

cards.title: Inject an Editable Objection-Busting Trust Block Under Add to Cart
cards.summary: Prompt Claude to add a reusable theme-editor block of trust icons and text directly below the buy buttons.
cards.use_when: Your product page lacks shipping, guarantee and returns reassurance near the add-to-cart button and you want it editable without an app.

cards.title: Generate a Full High-Converting Product Template from a Framework Document
cards.summary: Upload a product-page framework to Claude and have it code an entire reusable template with standard conversion sections.
cards.use_when: You want a structured, reusable PDP template beyond what your default theme ships with, and you already have a page anatomy/framework to follow.

cards.title: Clone a Competitor Design Element via Screenshot
cards.summary: Paste a screenshot of a competitor feature into Claude and have it build a matching, customizable component on your store.
cards.use_when: You spot a specific high-performing UI element (e.g. a 'Top Seller' badge on a swatch) on a competitor's store and want an equivalent on your PDP.

cards.title: Make Global Theme Edits (Cart Icon and Notification Bubble)
cards.summary: Prompt Claude to change sitewide theme utilities like the cart icon style, add a selection of preset icons, and customize the cart count bubble.
cards.use_when: You want storewide cosmetic/UX changes (cart icon, cart count color, add-to-cart feedback) that aren't exposed as template-level settings.

cards.title: Give Claude One Change at a Time, Not a Bundle
cards.summary: Split AI theme requests into single focused prompts, because bundling several changes risks partial or failed implementation.
cards.use_when: You are planning a series of theme or PDP edits and deciding how to sequence prompts.

cards.title: Manage Claude Usage Limits During Heavy Theme Coding
cards.summary: Plan for hitting Claude's usage limit and cooldown when running many theme edits.
cards.use_when: You are doing multi-hour AI theme work and want to avoid running out mid-task.

cards.title: Publish a Claude-Edited Theme and Maintain an Up-to-Date Working Copy
cards.summary: Publish your edited duplicate safely, then re-duplicate the live theme for the next round of edits.
cards.use_when: Your AI-edited theme or template is validated and you are ready to push it live.

cards.title: Clean a Fresh WordPress/WooCommerce Install
cards.summary: Remove identified demo content and unnecessary bundled plugins from a fresh store, then confirm its identity and timezone.
cards.use_when: Setting up a brand-new WooCommerce store on Hostinger and needing a clean baseline before adding products, pages or shipping rules.

cards.title: Pick the Right WooCommerce Product Type for Each Item
cards.summary: Map each catalog item to the correct WooCommerce product type - simple, variable, service, downloadable or affiliate - so inventory, pricing and checkout behave correctly.
cards.use_when: Adding products to a new WooCommerce store and choosing which product type template fits each item.

cards.title: Connect Stripe and PayPal with Test Mode First
cards.summary: Install the official Stripe and PayPal plugins, connect via API credentials, run sandbox transactions, and choose where express checkout buttons appear on the store.
cards.use_when: Enabling payment collection on a new WooCommerce store and deciding where Apple Pay / Google Pay buttons show.

cards.title: Set Up Flexible Table-Rate Shipping by Order Value
cards.summary: Use a table-rate shipping plugin to charge tiered flat rates based on cart price brackets and to unlock free shipping above a threshold, encouraging larger baskets.
cards.use_when: Configuring shipping charges and free-shipping thresholds in a new WooCommerce store, especially when rate should depend on order value rather than just weight.

cards.title: Configure Standard, Reduced and Zero Tax Rates
cards.summary: Assign products the correct tax class and set the store's price display so tax is shown consistently with your customer type.
cards.use_when: Setting up tax classes and price display in WooCommerce, particularly when you sell a mix of physical goods, reduced-rate items and digital products.

cards.title: Manually Configure US State Tax Rates in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Enter per-state standard tax rates manually in WooCommerce, using state codes and precise percentages sourced from a calculation service.
cards.use_when: Setting up tax collection in WooCommerce for US states where you need state-specific rates without an automated tax service.

cards.title: Create Legal Pages and Place Them in a Footer Menu
cards.summary: Generate Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions copy, publish them as WordPress pages, build a dedicated Legal menu and attach it to the footer.
cards.use_when: Publishing a new ecommerce store and needing Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions pages linked from every page for trust and compliance.

cards.title: Set Up Free Hosting, Domain and WordPress for a WooCommerce Store
cards.summary: End-to-end baseline setup: buy shared hosting, claim the free domain, install WordPress and pick the server region closest to your buying audience.
cards.use_when: Launching a brand-new store from scratch and you need hosting, a domain and WordPress installed before any product work can start.

cards.title: Clean a Fresh WordPress Install Before Building the Store
cards.summary: Remove default plugins, pages, posts and themes so the dashboard stays uncluttered and only the tools you actually need remain.
cards.use_when: Right after a fresh WordPress install, before installing WooCommerce, themes or page builders.

cards.title: Write a Site Title That Matches What Buyers Search
cards.summary: Name the store around the products and markets people actually search for, not around a generic welcome phrase.
cards.use_when: Setting the WordPress site title and tagline for a new store, or rewriting them when organic/paid traffic lands on generic pages.

cards.title: Install a Free Store Theme and Import a Starter Site
cards.summary: Use a free multipurpose theme with importable ecommerce starter sites to get product pages, categories and pages styled in minutes.
cards.use_when: Choosing the visual foundation of a new WooCommerce store when you want a working layout fast instead of designing pages from scratch.

cards.title: Install WooCommerce Manually and Complete the Setup Wizard
cards.summary: Add WooCommerce from the plugin repository and answer the onboarding questions so currency, industry and store address are correct.
cards.use_when: Building the store without importing a starter site, or when you need to re-run the WooCommerce setup wizard after import.

cards.title: Apply Global Brand Colors and a Logo Through the Customizer
cards.summary: Change the palette once in global color settings and have it propagate across the whole storefront, instead of editing each page.
cards.use_when: Rebranding an imported store template, adjusting colors for a client, or setting a logo/favicon before content launch.

cards.title: Shape the Header and Main Menu for Store Navigation
cards.summary: Trim and reorder the main menu, remove redundant entries, and style it to keep the sticky header usable on any page.
cards.use_when: Configuring site navigation right after importing a theme, especially before adding many product categories.

cards.title: Standardise Layout Widths for Store and Product Pages
cards.summary: Set a container width and a narrow single-product layout so product pages read comfortably on desktop.
cards.use_when: Imported template pages feel too wide or cramped and you want a consistent grid across shop, category and product pages.

cards.title: Create a Simple Product with Price, Sale Price, Stock and Categories
cards.summary: Configure a single-option product fully: description, short description, pricing, SKU, inventory, back-order policy, purchase note, images, categories and tags.
cards.use_when: Adding a physical product that has no size/colour variants — e.g. a couch, glasses, a cap — and you need the PDP to be complete before launch.

cards.title: Build Variable Products with Attributes, Swatches and Generated Variations
cards.summary: Define size/colour attributes once, generate every combination as a variation, then bulk-edit price and stock and set per-variation images.
cards.use_when: Listing apparel or any product with multiple sizes/colours and you want customers to select options visually on the product page.

cards.title: Create a Downloadable Digital Product with Unlimited Delivery
cards.summary: Sell a file (ebook, template, software) once and deliver it automatically an unlimited number of times to each buyer.
cards.use_when: Listing any non-physical deliverable where the same file serves every customer.

cards.title: List an Affiliate/External Product Without Shipping or Inventory
cards.summary: Promote a third-party product through your affiliate link by using the External/Affiliate product type, so the store shows it but checkout happens on the partner's site.
cards.use_when: Monetising storefront traffic with tools, themes or services you resell via an affiliate programme.

cards.title: Configure Currency and Store Locale in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Set currency, formatting and separators so all prices display correctly for the store's market.
cards.use_when: Right after setting the store's country, or when the store sells to a different market than its setup country.

cards.title: Use the Contrast Trick to Fix Mismatched Block Backgrounds
cards.summary: When a page section's background doesn't match the surrounding design, sample the correct colour and apply it in the block editor styles panel.
cards.use_when: After importing a template, a section on the homepage or landing page has a slightly-off background that breaks visual consistency.

cards.title: Set Up Manual US State Tax Rates with Inclusive/Exclusive Display
cards.summary: Enter per-state tax percentages manually and decide whether shop prices show excluding tax while checkout shows tax inclusive.
cards.use_when: Selling to US customers where you must charge state-level sales tax, especially in a B2B/B2C hybrid store.

cards.title: Set Shipping Cost Brackets and a Free-Shipping Threshold in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Use a shipping plugin's conditions to charge by cart-price bracket and unlock free shipping above a threshold.
cards.use_when: Configuring shipping zones and rates for a physical-goods store where you want shipping cost to scale with order value.

cards.title: Create WooCommerce affiliate products with external/affiliate product type
cards.summary: Set up an affiliate product in WooCommerce by switching product type to external/affiliate, adding your affiliate link and price label, so you earn commission without holding inventory.
cards.use_when: Merchandising: you want to add a partner tool, brand or recommended gear to your catalog and earn affiliate commission on click-through rather than selling stocked goods.

cards.title: Add WooCommerce upsells (product page) vs cross-sells (cart)
cards.summary: Configure upsells to appear on a product page and cross-sells in the cart, and understand that cross-sells are only triggered by the specific product in the cart.
cards.use_when: Merchandising / AOV: you want to lift average order value by recommending complementary products at the product page or in the cart.

cards.title: Customize shop look with fonts, spacing and archive layout
cards.summary: Use the WordPress customizer typography and WooCommerce product archive settings to control fonts, product card layout, spacing and colors, especially to lift the heavy title area above the product grid.
cards.use_when: PDP/landing page and storefront design: your product archive looks cluttered or off-brand and you want to tighten the top area and standardize typography before running traffic.

cards.title: Sell to specific countries and set flexible table-rate shipping by price tiers
cards.summary: Restrict selling/shipping to specific countries and configure the Flexible Shipping (table-rate) plugin to charge shipping based on cart price tiers, with a free-shipping threshold.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment / pricing: you ship to a limited set of countries and want shipping cost that scales with order value instead of a flat rate.

cards.title: Configure tax rates by country, state and product class
cards.summary: Enable WooCommerce taxes, build standard/reduced/zero rate classes, assign product tax classes, and choose whether displayed prices include tax — matching the whole customer journey.
cards.use_when: Pricing/checkout: you sell physical, book/reduced and digital products across multiple countries and need tax to calculate correctly and display consistently.

cards.title: Generate legal pages content and add them to the footer menu
cards.summary: Draft the legal pages you need (privacy, terms, returns, etc.) with an AI assistant and publish them into a footer legal menu so they are linked from every page.
cards.use_when: Store setup: you are preparing to launch and need compliant legal pages without paying for legal drafting, and want them discoverable sitewide.

cards.title: Enable card, PayPal and wallet payments (Stripe + PayPal) and test the flow
cards.summary: Install the WooCommerce Stripe gateway to accept cards and wallets, add PayPal as a secondary method, run a test-mode order, then flip to live and simplify the checkout fields.
cards.use_when: Checkout: you are launching a store and need working card, PayPal and wallet payment methods before sending real traffic.

cards.title: Handle incoming orders and manage WooCommerce order statuses
cards.summary: Use order statuses to move an order from Processing to Completed when physical goods ship, or to Cancelled/Refunded as needed, which triggers the appropriate customer emails.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: you have live orders and need a repeatable process for processing, shipping, completing or refunding them.

cards.title: Brand transactional order emails (colors, logo, copy)
cards.summary: Style and edit WooCommerce customer emails — colors, logo, headings and body copy — so transactional messages match the store's branding and read clearly.
cards.use_when: Retention / post-purchase: your order confirmation emails look generic and you want them consistent with your brand and better worded.

cards.title: Connect OmniSend to WooCommerce and brand the account
cards.summary: Install the OmniSend plugin to sync a WooCommerce store with an email platform so you can build lists, send campaigns and track email-attributed revenue.
cards.use_when: Retention/acquisition: you want an email list and marketing automation tied to your store, plus revenue attribution from email.

cards.title: Build a discount opt-in pop-up to grow the email list
cards.summary: Create an OmniSend opt-in form that offers a first-order discount in exchange for name and email, control when it triggers, and match it to the store's styling.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/retention: you want to capture emails on-site by offering a discount pop-up instead of relying only on paid traffic.

cards.title: Set up a welcome automation with a unique per-person discount code
cards.summary: Build an OmniSend welcome workflow triggered by the signup form that sends a sequence of emails containing a unique single-use discount code, and reuse that same code across the sequence.
cards.use_when: Retention: after a visitor subscribes, you want an automated welcome sequence that delivers a personal discount and nudges a first purchase.

cards.title: Welcome Email Series with Unique Per-Subscriber Coupon Codes
cards.summary: Build a multi-email welcome automation where each subscriber receives a personally generated single-use discount code.
cards.use_when: You are setting up the opt-in to first-purchase email flow and want a personal, trackable discount instead of one shared public code.

cards.title: Split Testing Email Subject Lines and Content to Lift Revenue
cards.summary: Use drag-and-drop A/B split testing on emails to find subject lines and content that increase opens and sales.
cards.use_when: You have an established email flow or campaign and want to improve open rates or revenue per send.

cards.title: Abandoned Cart Email Triggered by Cart Inactivity
cards.summary: Set up an automation that emails shoppers who add an item to cart but do not purchase within a defined inactivity window.
cards.use_when: You want to recover checkout/cart abandonment without manual outreach.

cards.title: Behavioral and Value-Based Subscriber Segments Feeding Targeted Automations
cards.summary: Create segments from email engagement, purchase behavior, region, and value, then trigger tailored workflows when contacts enter a segment.
cards.use_when: You want to send different offers to different customer groups automatically rather than one list-wide campaign.

cards.title: Custom Branded Order Confirmation Email Replacing the Default
cards.summary: Create a styled order confirmation workflow so customers receive a better-looking confirmation than the default store email.
cards.use_when: Your default WooCommerce order confirmation looks generic and you want a branded post-purchase touchpoint.

cards.title: Revenue Attribution: Separating Platform-Driven Sales from Total Store Revenue
cards.summary: Use your email/automation platform's tracking to see how much revenue is directly driven by automations versus the store as a whole.
cards.use_when: You want to judge whether your email automations and opt-in offers are actually driving revenue before investing further.

cards.title: Swap Shared Discount Codes for Unique, Single-Use, Time-Limited Codes
cards.summary: Use per-contact, expiry-limited, single-use coupon codes so discounts can be tracked to individuals and cannot be reused.
cards.use_when: You are designing an opt-in incentive and want protection against code sharing and clearer attribution.

cards.title: Editing Homepage Content, Product Blocks and Prices in the Site Editor
cards.summary: Directly edit homepage text, images, product references, prices and styling in the WordPress block editor by clicking and adjusting right-side settings.
cards.use_when: You need to update your store homepage hero, featured product blocks, or promotional text without a developer.

cards.title: Making the Header, Menu and Off-Canvas Mobile View Responsive
cards.summary: Use the editor's tablet/mobile preview to fix header, menu, logo and icon styling so the site works on all devices.
cards.use_when: Your site looks broken on tablet or mobile and you need to correct layout and styling for smaller screens.

cards.title: Optional Channels: Texts and Push Notifications Alongside Email
cards.summary: Extend your automation workflows to SMS and push notifications when you have the subscriber's contact details.
cards.use_when: Your list includes phone numbers or app/device access and you want to reach people beyond the inbox.

cards.title: Using Tags to Conditionally Gate Automation Emails
cards.summary: Apply tags to contacts and use them as conditions so emails only send to appropriately grouped people.
cards.use_when: You want certain workflow emails to fire only for a subsection of subscribers (e.g., a specific offer or cohort).
